sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants with a prayer to quash the charge-sheet dated 12.05.2023 and cognizance order dated 03.07.2023 as well as entire proceedings of Case No. 884 of 2023 (State Vs. Nikhil and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.
618 of 2022, under Section 420 IPC, Police Station Garhmukteshwar, District Hapur, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Jr. Div.)/ Judicial Magistrate, Garhmukteshwar, Hapur.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Nikhil And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the allegations made in the FIR, it is alleged that the applicants, with fraudulent intention to cheat the Government, had remarried each other and had taken the benefits granted by the State Government.

Subsequently, it was revealed that in fact, they were already married and just with intention to cheat and swindle the amount of Rs.51,000/- given as aid by the State Government,
they have remarried.
4.

Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that even taking the entire allegations made in the FIR as well as statement of the witnesses recorded under Sections 161 CrPC, no offence,
complained of, is made out against the applicants and as such, entire prosecution case is liable to be quashed.
He has pointed out certain documents and statements in support of his contention.

5. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the said prayer and has supported the impugned cognizance order and has submitted that the applicants, being already married, had remarried to each other and just with intention to cheat, had swindled the amount of Rs.51,000/-
from the State Government.

6. Learned AGA has further submitted that from perusal of the allegations made in the FIR and the material collected during the course of investigation, prima facie offence is clearly made out against the applicants and as such, impugned cognizance order and entire proceedings cannot be quashed.
7.
From perusal of the material on record and looking into the facts of the case, at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicants.

All the submissions made at the bar relate to the disputed questions of fact, which cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
8.

At this stage, disputed question of fact cannot be considered, therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1960 SC 866,
State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cri.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P. Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cri.) 192 and lastly Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another,
(Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cri.) 283, the prayer for quashing the impugned cognizance order and entire proceedings is refused.
